translations.text: Any man who disobeys you and does not listen to your words, whatever command you give him, shall die. Only be strong and courageous.

Joshua son of Nun sent two young men from Shittim to spy out the land secretly, saying, “Go and spy out the land and Jericho.” The two young men went to Jericho, entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and lodged there.

“Look, we will enter a part of your city. You shall put up a scarlet cord as a sign and tie it to the window through which you let us down. Gather your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household to you in this house.”
When the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth enter the water of the Jordan, the water flowing down from above shall cease and stand in a single heap.
Take for yourself twelve men from that people, one man from each tribe.
Joshua called twelve men from among the distinguished men of the Israelites, one from each tribe.
So that they may stand as a lasting sign for you, when your son asks you in days to come, “What do these stones mean to you?”
So that all the nations of the earth may know that the Lord’s power is mighty, and so that you may worship the Lord your God at all times.

When he had instructed the people, the seven priests who carried the seven sacred trumpets were likewise to pass before the Lord and sound them loudly, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord was to go behind them.

Joshua gave the people a command, saying, “Do not shout, let no one hear your voice, and let no word come out of your mouth until the day when he himself gives the signal to shout. Then you shall shout.”
The Lord said to Joshua, “Stand up! Why are you lying fallen on your face?”

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or alarmed. Take all the fighting men with you, rise, and go up to Ai. Look, I am giving into your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.”
“I and all the people with me will approach the city. When the inhabitants of Ai come out against us as they did before, we will flee before them.”
All the people of the land hurried to pursue them and pressed on after the Israelites, and they went away from the city.
No one remained in Ai or Bethel who did not press on after Israel. They left the city open and rushed after Israel.
They all came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
All the leaders said to all the people, “We swore an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel, and we cannot break our word to them.”
On that day he appointed them to be woodcutters and water carriers for all the people and for the altar of God, down to this day, at the place the Lord would choose.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I will deliver them into your hands, and not one of them will be able to stand against you.”
The Lord threw them into terror before Israel and struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon. They pursued them along the road down from Beth-horon and slaughtered them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before the Israelites down the slope of Beth-horon, the Lord hurled hailstones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword in battle.
Joshua was informed, and they said, “The five kings have been found hiding in the cave there at Makkedah.”
When Joshua and all the Israelites had finished slaughtering them in a very great slaughter, until they were completely destroyed, the survivors who escaped from among them entered fortified cities.
All the people returned unharmed to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah, and not one of the Israelites muttered with his tongue.
When Jabin king of Hazor heard this, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings of Great Sidon in the hill country, in Rabbah opposite Chinnereth, in the plain, in Naphoth-dor, and along the coast.
They came out, with their kings accompanying them, and a great army, as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
All those kings assembled and came together, and they camped together beside the waters of Merom to wage war against Israel.
Joshua captured all the cities of those kingdoms and their kings, struck them down with the edge of the sword, and destroyed them, just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded them.
Joshua took the whole land, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua gave it to Israel as an inheritance by lot according to their tribes. And the land rested from war.

And the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, the Arabah as far as the sea, as far as the Salt Sea on the east, by the road to Beth-jeshimoth, and from Teman, which lies below the slopes of Pisgah.
The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one.
This is the inheritance of the descendants of Gad according to their clans, with their cities and their surrounding lands.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities.

The descendants of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You yourself know what the Lord said to Moses the man of God concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea.”
And the boundaries pass to the ascent of Akrabbim, go around Zin, ascend from the south to Kadesh-barnea, go out to Hezron, extend past Addar, and turn around to the west of Kadesh.
They proceed to Azmon and extend as far as the ravine of Egypt, and the boundary ends at the sea. These are their southern boundaries.
And Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah: sixteen cities and their villages.
And the boundary shall descend from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, and their villages shall pass by Jericho and extend to the Jordan.

From Tappuah the boundary shall pass westward to the ravine of Kanah, and its endpoint shall be at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim according to their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters. These are the names of Zelophehad’s daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They stood before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the leaders, and said, “God commanded through Moses that an inheritance be given to us among our brothers.” And he gave them an inheritance, by the Lord’s command, among their father’s brothers.

The descendants of Joseph said, “The hill country of Ephraim is not enough for us, and there are the very best horses and weapons belonging to every Canaanite who lives in my land alongside me, in Beth-shean and its villages and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
And you shall divide the land into seven parts and bring them here to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the Lord our God.
And the southern border begins at the edge of Kiriath-jearim, and the boundaries pass to Gai and extend to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
And they cross northward and pass to the spring at Shemesh, and turn toward Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and descend to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
And they pass behind Beth-arabah on the north and descend to the Arabah.
And the Jordan forms the boundary on the eastern side. This is the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin, with their boundaries all around, according to their clans.
And the second lot fell to Simeon, to the tribe of the descendants of Simeon according to their clans, and their inheritance was within the allotment of the descendants of Judah.
And they turn from Sarid eastward toward Beth-shemesh, to the boundary of Chisloth-tabor, and pass to Daberath and go up to Japhia.
And Rabbith and Kishion and Aemes.

These are the portions that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel divided by lot at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony. And they went to inspect the land.

And he shall live in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the high priest who serves in those days dies. Then the killer shall return and come to his own place and his own house, to the city from which he fled.
And to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, a city of refuge for a killer, with its pasturelands, and Libnah with its pasturelands.

And to the descendants of Gershon, from the clans of the Levites, they gave from the half-tribe of Manasseh cities set apart for killers: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands—two cities.
And from the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its pasturelands, and Abdon with its pasturelands.
And you have not abandoned your brothers for all those days and even longer, up to this present day, and you have kept the commandments of the Lord your God.

And to half the tribe of Manasseh Moses gave land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land among their brothers along the seacoast. And when Joshua sent them away to their homes, he blessed them.
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the commanders of thousands, saying:
And we said, ‘Let us do this: build this altar, not for burnt offerings and not for sacrifices.’
But if you turn back and join the nations that remain among you, and intermarry with them, and mingle with them and they with you,
And I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him throughout the land of the Canaanites, and multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac.

But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers who were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But I and my household will serve the Lord, for he is holy.

For the Lord our God himself brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed those great signs for us, and protected us along the entire way we traveled and among all the nations through which we passed.
